summary: This bill adds a federal crime to title 49 that fines and imprisons for up to 20 years any person who intentionally causes or arranges a collision between a motor vehicle and a commercial motor vehicle, with a minimum 20-year sentence if serious injury or death results, unless the person has already been convicted or acquitted under state law for the same act.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates new federal criminal penalties but does not authorize or appropriate any spending, nor does it expand or reduce government programs. Any enforcement costs would be incidental and minimal.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill has no connection to healthcare policy, insurance mandates, or medical coverage.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions related to immigration, borders, visas, or enforcement of immigration law.
The legislation does not address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No impact on military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces.
No environmental regulations, climate provisions, or energy policy changes.
The bill does not modify welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.
No provisions concerning schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.

The bill adds a new federal criminal offense for staging collisions with commercial motor vehicles, imposing substantial prison terms (up to 20 years, or a minimum of 20 years if serious injury or death results). This directly strengthens criminal penalties and enforcement in the area of insurance fraud involving staged accidents, aligning with tougher sentencing rather than rehabilitation-focused reforms.
No provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill has no fiscal measures that would affect deficits or debt reduction strategies.
No content related to LGBTQ protections or legal status.
No foreign aid authorizations or reductions.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance provisions.
No data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance measures.
The bill does not address worker rights, union organizing, or employer obligations.
No provisions involving religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
